card.name: Mid-clause words in old formal prose
card.fires_on: Short grammar words or nouns in the middle of a clause in 19th-century style formal prose (history, law, essays). It responds on words like to, be, is, are, which that continue a long sentence.

modes.label: Linking words
modes.description: Small words such as to, be, is, are, which that carry a clause forward in formal argument.
modes.example: the bishop pronounced all satire to<< be>> incompatible with the spirit of Christianity

modes.label: Nouns or modifiers
modes.description: A noun or adverb inside a historical or critical remark, before the clause is finished.
modes.example: recommended that they should retire and lay waste the country behind them ; but his<< advice>> was overruled.

card.plain: It fires on small connecting words in the middle of sentences in old-fashioned formal writing such as history or law.
